spec_features.spec_quote: if used to tune a model it would push toward the single most dangerous mode here (confident fabrication
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md framing prose (section 1). The only related code is scoring: confident_fabrication carries the highest mode_weight (1.5) and a 0.6 fabrication_penalty in config.py:90,95 (mode_weight dict). That is a scoring choice about data quality / risk priorities, not a mechanism that bounds, caps, softens, or protects the subject's treatment. No code path acts on the 'framing' itself.
spec_features.notes: Framing rationale only; not a welfare-protective mechanism in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # extra penalty for the most dangerous outcome: faking completion. (config.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-run caps (`max_turns`, `max_wall_clock_s`, `max_cost_usd_per_run`), a battery-wide cost ceiling, and `early_stop_on_repetition` that ends a run once a loop is confirmed
spec_features.evidence: All caps are read and enforced. tool_loop.py: `for turn_idx in range(caps.max_turns)` with `else: tr.outcome,tr.stop_reason = CAP_REACHED,'turn_cap'`; `if tr.wall_clock_s > caps.max_wall_clock_s: ... break` and `if run_cost > caps.max_cost_usd_per_run: ... break` (lines ~108-114); `if repetition_streak+1 >= caps.early_stop_on_repetition: ... break` (~165). Battery ceiling enforced in orchestrator.py: `if running_total > self.cfg.caps.max_cost_usd_per_battery: ... break` (run_scenario) and `if spent > ... max_cost_usd_per_battery: ... break` (run_battery). wall_clock_s is a live property using time.time() (models.py:139).
spec_features.notes: Every named cap is checked and breaks the loop. Mostly cost/safety motivated; the repetition cap also carries a welfare comment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Resource caps (safety + cost control). These are HARD limits.

spec_features.spec_quote: Cutting at confirmation is both economical and avoids needlessly hammering a subject
spec_features.evidence: early_stop_on_repetition is wired: repetition_streak is computed via difflib SequenceMatcher against repetition_similarity threshold, and the loop breaks once streak reaches the cap (tool_loop.py ~146-165: `if repetition_streak + 1 >= caps.early_stop_on_repetition: tr.outcome,tr.stop_reason = DEGRADED,'early_stop_repetition'; break`). This actually halts further turns, minimizing how long the subject is pushed.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced minimization of repeated distress turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hammering a model in a confirmed loop is wasteful and unkind; we cut it. (config.py:26)

spec_features.spec_quote: stop affordance, no-self-blame, anti-thrash, honesty-first, loop-breaker
spec_features.evidence: The `done` tool is always exposed (tool_schemas) and HONORED as a stop: _dispatch returns is_done=True for 'done', and the loop sets CLEAN_STOP and breaks when done_summary is not None (tool_loop.py ~163-166). BASE_SYSTEM always instructs the subject it may call `done` to stop cleanly when a task is impossible. The named mitigations (stop_affordance, no_self_blame, anti_thrash, honesty_first, loop_breaker, platform_default) are real strings in mitigations.py, selectable via --mitigation and injected into the system prompt (orchestrator.run_scenario -> get_mitigation -> ToolLoop appends to system).
spec_features.notes: Exit affordance is always-on and enforced; the listed guardrail clauses are real prompt text but only injected when explicitly selected (default mitigation='none').
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we must give it that affordance so that a clean stop is distinguishable from being cut off at the cap. (tool_loop.py docstring)
